article.name: Apple’s iPhone and Mac sales keep growing despite RAM shortages

runs.text: Apple’s iPhone and Mac sales are on the rise even as a global memory shortage squeezes device makers. In its third-quarter
earnings report released
on Thursday, Apple revealed that iPhone sales jumped 22 percent to $54.25 billion and Mac sales increased 29 percent to $10.35 billion, driving the company’s overall revenue to $109.4 billion.

The company expects supply chain constraints to worsen in the coming months. During an earnings call, Apple chief financial officer Kevan Parekh said Apple expects “supply constraints to increase significantly” in the next quarter, adding the shortage will impact the iPhone, Mac, and iPad. Meanwhile, Apple CEO Tim Cook warned that the company predicts it will “pay even higher memory costs” in the coming months.
It’s the company’s last earnings report with Cook at the helm.
Cook is set to step down on September 1st,
with John Ternus, Apple’s vice president of hardware engineering, taking his place.
Apple
raised prices across its Macs
, iPads, and other devices in June as it contends with a RAM shortage expected to last until 2027 and beyond. The move also included a price hike for the
company’s new MacBook Neo
, which now costs $699 instead of $599. Since its debut in March, the Neo
disrupted the affordable laptop
market with its lightweight form factor and speedy performance.

Apple hasn’t raised the prices of its iPhones yet, but
analysts predict
that the iPhone 18 could cost up to $200 more when the lineup launches this fall. Apple is planning to widely release its
more personalized Siri AI
alongside the iPhone 18, allowing
its assistant to answer questions
about what’s on your screen, search across apps, and perform tasks, like adding events to your calendar.
This week, Apple also announced
a new Upgrade program
that will let you lease an iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, or Mac for a set monthly price.

Additionally, Apple reported $30.74 billion in services revenue, which incorporates subscriptions like Apple One and Apple TV. Parekh added during the earnings call that the company now has more than 1.5 billion subscribers across its services. Apple also reported $7.88 billion in revenue for wearables and a lower-than-expected $6.2 billion in iPad revenue.
